title: "Fit MOSM GP to 2-band synthetic example"
format: 
  html:
    embed-resources: true
---

This notebook contains the workflow for:

- loading groundtruth 2-band (MOGP) time-series,
- fitting a multicomponent MOSM GP model,
- drawing posterior predictive samples,
- visualising the posteriors .

```{r message=FALSE}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)
library(readr)
library(glue)
library(jsonlite)

register_knitr_engine(override = FALSE)

theme_set(theme_bw())
color_scheme_set("viridis")

source(here("mogp-utils.R"))

filename_stub <- "D2-Q3-seed2312-n300-mnar0.3-noise0.5"

EXECUTE_SAMPLING <- FALSE

N_CHAINS <- 4
N_WARMUP <- 500
N_SAMPLES <- 500

# Function estimates the mode of a sample
estimate_mode <- function(x) {
  d <- density(x, n = 2^6)
  d$x[which.max(d$y)]
}
```

```{r}
input_df <- read_csv(
  here("data", glue("{filename_stub}-sim.csv")), 
  col_types = "dddf",
  show_col_types = FALSE)

input_params <- read_json(
  here("data", glue("{filename_stub}-param.json")), 
  simplifyVector = TRUE)

input_df |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = t, y = y, colour = factor(d)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymax = y + y_se, ymin = y - y_se), colour = "black") +
  geom_point() +
  labs(colour = "Band", title = glue("M = {NROW(input_df)}"))
```

```{r}
input_params
```

# Model Fitting

```{r}
stan_model <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "mosmgp-D2-Q.stan"))
```

## Sampling

```{r}
D <- 2
Q <- 3 

band1_df <- filter(input_df, d == 1)
band1_mean <- mean(band1_df$y)
band1_sd <- sd(band1_df$y)

band2_df <- filter(input_df, d == 2)
band2_mean <- mean(band2_df$y)
band2_sd <- sd(band2_df$y)

ell_min <- median(  diff( sort(input_df$t) )  )
ell_max <- diff(range(input_df$t))
ell_loc <- log(sqrt(ell_min * ell_max)) # for log-normal prior

data_list <- list(
  Q = Q,
  N1 = length(band1_df$t),
  N2 = length(band2_df$t),
  t1 = band1_df$t,
  t2 = band2_df$t,
  y1 = (band1_df$y - band1_mean)/band1_sd, # standardised
  y2 = (band2_df$y - band2_mean)/band2_sd,
  y1_se = band1_df$y_se/band1_sd,
  y2_se = band2_df$y_se/band2_sd,
  ell_min = ell_min,
  ell_max = ell_max,
  ell_loc = ell_loc,
  ell_scale = 1,
  v_scale = 1, # data has been standardised
  mu_scale = 3
)
```

```{r}
ell_min
ell_max
ell_loc
```

### Priors

$$w^2 = \frac{v}{\sqrt{2 \pi \Sigma}}, \quad \Sigma = \frac{1}{\ell^2}$$


$$
v \sim \mathcal{N}_+(0, v_\textrm{scale}), \quad \mu \sim \mathcal{N}_+(0, \mu_\textrm{scale}), \quad \ell \sim \mathrm{lognormal}(\ell_\textrm{loc}, \ell_\textrm{scale}), \quad \theta_2 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1), \quad \phi_2 \sim \mathrm{U}[-\pi, \pi]
$$

$$v_\textrm{scale} = 1, \quad \mu_\textrm{scale} = 3, \quad \ell_\textrm{loc} = \log(\sqrt{\ell_\textrm{min}\times \ell_\textrm{max}}, \quad \ell_\textrm{scale} = 1, $$

```{r}
format(start_time <- Sys.time())

if (EXECUTE_SAMPLING) {
  init_fun <- function() {
    list(
      mu1 = c(0.79, 2.72, 0.2) + rnorm(Q, 0, 0.1),
      mu2 = c(0.93, 2.81, 0.19) + rnorm(Q, 0, 0.1)
    )
  }

  output <- stan_model$sample(
    data = data_list,
    #init = init_fun,
    chains = N_CHAINS,
    parallel_chains = N_CHAINS,
    iter_warmup = N_WARMUP,
    iter_sampling = N_SAMPLES,
    refresh = 500,
    show_exceptions = FALSE,
    show_messages = TRUE
  )
  
  output$save_object(
    here("RDS", glue("{filename_stub}_mosmgp-D{D}-Q{Q}.RDS")))
  
} else {
  output <- readRDS(
    here("RDS", glue("{filename_stub}_mosmgp-D{D}-Q{Q}.RDS")))
}

format(finish_time <- Sys.time())
difftime(finish_time, start_time)  
```

## Posterior Predictive Check

```{r}
n_star <- 200
ts1 <- seq(from = 0, to = 10, length.out = n_star)
ts2 <- ts1

# Draw posterior predictive samples using a particular posterior draw
post_draw <- as.data.frame(output_draws[sample.int(nrow(output_draws_mat), 1),])

pp_draw <- pred_D2_Q_draw(post_draw, 
                          Q = Q, 
                          t1 = band1_df$t, t2 = band2_df$t, 
                          y1 = band1_df$y, y2 = band2_df$y, 
                          y1_se = band1_df$y_se, y2_se = band2_df$y_se, 
                          ts1 = ts1, ts2 = ts2)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = pp_draw, aes(x = ts, y = fs, colour = d)) +
  geom_point(data = input_df, aes(x = t, y = y, fill = d), shape = 21, size = 1.5) +
  labs(colour = "Band")
```

```{r}
pp_draws <- pred_D2_Q(draws = output_draws, 
                      Q = Q,
                      t1 = band1_df$t, 
                      t2 = band2_df$t, 
                      y1 = band1_df$y, 
                      y2 = band2_df$y, 
                      y1_se = band1_df$y_se, 
                      y2_se = band2_df$y_se, 
                      ts1 = ts1, 
                      ts2 = ts2, 
                      n_draws = 100)

pp_draws |> 
  summarise(.by = c(d, ts),
            Mean = mean(fs),
            Q2.5 = quantile(fs, probs = 0.025),
            Q97.5 = quantile(fs, probs = 0.975),
            Q16 = quantile(fs, probs = 0.16),
            Q84 = quantile(fs, probs = 0.84)) |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = ts, fill = d) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q2.5, ymax = Q97.5, alpha = "95%")) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q16, ymax = Q84, alpha = "68%")) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = d, y = Mean)) +
  geom_point(data = input_df, aes(x = t, y = y, fill = d), shape = 21, size = 1) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`95%` = 0.2, `68%` = 0.5)) +
  labs(colour = "Band", fill = "Band", y = "f", x = "t", alpha = "Quantile") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Interpreting $\mu$s

```{r}
mus <- as.data.frame(output_draws) |> 
  select(matches("mu"), -.draw) |> 
  colMeans() |> 
  matrix(ncol = 2)
mus
```

Each cell indicates the dominant oscillation frequency (radians/unit time) of the q-th (row) component in the i-th (column) band.

Cells are labelled in ordered by $\mu$ therefore highest frequency component in band 1 has frequency 2.88 radians per unit time.

Where each mu differs between bands (in all components in this case), the cross-covariance has a frequency that is the variance weighted average of the two, i.e., $\mu_{ij}$ is frequency of the product of two Gaussians pulled towards the one with the narrower peak.

As the $\mu$s become more separated, the component is really two unrelated oscillators. In such cases, $\theta$ and $\phi$ are no longer meaningful and just reflect their priors.


# Interpreting $\theta$s

Entry theta[q, i] is band `i`’s (column) time shift within component `q` (row).

The delay between bands 1 and 2 in component q is `theta[q, 1] − theta[q, 2]`.

A delay is only meaningful relative to how fast the cross-covariance decays.

```{r}
thetas <- as.data.frame(output_draws) |> 
  select(matches("theta"), -.draw) |> 
  colMeans() |> 
  matrix(ncol = 2)
thetas
```

```{r}
phis <- as.data.frame(output_draws) |> 
  select(matches("phi"), -.draw) |> 
  colMeans() |> 
  matrix(ncol = 2)
phis
```

For example, `theta[1,2]` = 0.040, means that in component 1, the time shift between band 2 and band 1 is 0.040. Alternatively, component 2 in band 1 at time $t$ lines up with band 2 at $t - 0.040$.


A time shift of $\theta$ corresponds to a phase shift of $\mu_{ij} \times \theta_{ij} + \phi_{ij}$ radians, i.e., the net phase offset at that frequency.


```{r}
mus * thetas + phis
```

# Interpreting $\Sigma$s

$\Sigma$s refer to the widths of the bumps in the spectral domain centred at the $\mu$s.

Coherence length is $\ell = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Sigma}}$. There cannot be a stable cross-covariance, if two oscillators already drift out of phase within just one coherence length. Long coherence lengths (narrow spectral peaks) make the $\mu$ gap matter more, short coherence lengths (broad spectral peaks) make the gap matter less.

If cross-covariance is zero, then there's insufficient information to estimate $\theta$ or $\phi$. $\mu$s are still identifiable but this component is really two unrelated oscillators, i.e., there is no shared signal to be delayed between bands.

```{r}
Sigmas <- as.data.frame(output_draws) |> 
  select(matches("Sigma"), -.draw) |> 
  colMeans() |> 
  sqrt() |> 
  matrix(ncol = 2)
Sigmas
```

# Interpreting $w$

```{r}
ws <- as.data.frame(output_draws) |> 
  select(matches("w"), -.draw) |> 
  colMeans() |> 
  sqrt() |> 
  matrix(ncol = 2)
ws
```

If $w$ was near zero (not in this case), then $\theta$ and $\phi$ for that component revert to their prior.
